column1: # Halo 5 first person arms -> Halo CE first person arms (frame bone24 rig).
# Tab separated. Target names may list alternatives separated by '|' (the first one found in the scene is used).
# bone   <h5 node>  <target node>  <h5 aim child>  <target aim child>  <up: world|palm_l|palm_r>  [root]
#        The aim child gives the bone direction; '-' uses the direction from the parent joint (finger tips).
#        'root' bones follow the Halo 5 node position; the others keep the target bone lengths.
# palm   <side>  <h5 wrist> <h5 middle> <h5 index> <h5 ring>  <target wrist> <target middle> <target index> <target ring>
#        Palm normal = (middle - wrist) x (index - ring): the twist reference shared by both skeletons.
#        Use fingers parented straight to the wrist: a Halo 5 pinky hangs from an animated metacarpal (b_*_pinky0).
# ik     <side>  <h5 upperarm> <h5 forearm> <h5 hand>  <target upperarm> <target forearm> <target hand>
#        Two-bone IK puts the target wrist where the Halo 5 wrist is; the Halo 5 elbow gives the bend direction.
#        Halo 5 weapon nodes keep their placement relative to the hand.
#        With 'Remove camera motion', every pose is taken relative to this node.
#        Constant correction in degrees about the target bone's local axes (X, then Y, then Z), like rotating
#        it in 'Local' in 3ds Max. For bones whose anatomy differs between the two rigs (thumbs).
